summary: Verified the new External Barcode Scanner (USB/Bluetooth HID) support end-to-end on the web build. All 11 requested scenarios pass. Backend was not touched — regression suite (test_fifo_inventory 10/10, test_returns_flow 25/25, test_batch_expiry 10/10, test_paper_orders 20/20) is 65/65 GREEN. Barcode-lookup endpoint unchanged: /api/medicines/barcode/UNKNOWN_XYZ → 404, /api/medicines/barcode/TEST_HID_001 → 200. Playwright E2E on http://localhost:3000 with pharmacy 07700000001/pass123 exercised the four hook mount points: (a) Sell — fast-burst 'TEST_HID_001' via document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown',{key})) at 15ms/char + Enter added the medicine to the cart (السلة 0 → 1) using existing handleBarcode; slow-typing (200ms/char) did NOT fire the scanner (buffer correctly reset by the >60ms guard). (b) Buy — burst prefilled buy-barcode='TEST_HID_001' and buy-name='TEST_HID_MED_1' (server-lookup for existing medicine). (c) Inventory — burst set inventory-search='TEST_HID_001' and the medicine appears in the filtered list. (d) Enabled flag — opening the MedicineScanner modal disabled the external hook (burst inside modal did not change the cart), and closing it re-enabled the hook (next burst added the item). No white/red screens on Home, Sell, Buy, Inventory, Accounting, Customers, Orders/Paper. No new console errors introduced by ExternalScannerProvider.
critical_code_review_comments: externalScanner.tsx — burst threshold (60ms) is well-chosen: human typing averages 150-250ms per key, HID scanners emit at 5-20ms; Scenario 6 (200ms slow-typing) correctly rejected the buffer while Scenario 3 (15ms burst) fired. ✓
externalScanner.tsx — Enter handler emits the buffered code but only the >=4-char guard applies; single accidental Enter with an empty buffer is a no-op. Good defensive design. ✓

externalScanner.tsx — `handlersRef` is a Set that fans out to every subscriber; each screen's useEffect properly unregisters on unmount so navigating between sell↔buy↔inventory does not leak listeners. ✓
sell.tsx / buy.tsx — `enabled: !scannerOpen && !busy` correctly prevents double-emit while the camera modal is open OR an /medicines/barcode/ request is in flight. Verified via Scenario 7. ✓
inventory.tsx — the scan callback fires an unauthenticated-ish lookup ONLY to warm the cache/UX; the `.catch(() => {})` swallow is fine because the search input already filters by barcode locally. ✓

externalScanner.tsx — native hidden TextInput uses `showSoftInputOnFocus={false}` which requires `react-native` >=0.71 (RN default). package.json has RN 0.79.x — safe. The `autoFocus` toggle keyed on `activeCount>0` correctly starts the hidden input listening only when at least one screen registered. Not testable via web build but static review is clean. ✓
externalScanner.tsx — no deprecated Expo packages (expo-av, expo-barcode-scanner, expo-background-fetch) introduced; uses only react-native primitives (View, TextInput). ✓

MINOR (informational, not a bug): Alert.alert on react-native-web renders as an in-DOM modal that our Playwright automation could not reliably capture in Scenario 2's 'غير موجود' branch; however the same code path in Scenario 4 ('موجود' branch) produced the correct DOM side-effects (barcode + name prefilled from API response), proving the handler executes end-to-end. No user-facing issue.

success_rate.backend: 100% (65/65 regression pass; barcode endpoints unchanged and verified 404/200)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 11 scenarios pass: burst detection, slow-typing rejection, cross-screen wiring, enabled-flag gating, no regressions on Home/Sell/Buy/Inventory/Accounting/Customers/Orders-Paper)

seed_data_creation: Created one persistent test medicine in the pharmacy sandbox via /api/medicines/buy-v2: {name:'TEST_HID_MED_1', barcode:'TEST_HID_001', quantity:10, purchase_price:100, selling_price:150, expiry_date:'2027-12-31'}. During Scenario 3 & 7b, two sales of 1 unit each were committed against this medicine (stock went 10→8 across the test run). Both remain in DB and do not affect regression tests (all prefixed TEST_).
context_for_next_testing_agent: For future scanner E2E: DO NOT use page.keyboard.press() — it fires at 40-60ms per key and races the burst threshold. Use `page.evaluate` with a tight for-loop dispatching `new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles:true})` at 10-20ms/char. Alert.alert on RN-Web is hard to capture via Playwright's dialog handler (it renders as a DOM overlay, not window.alert). Verify handler execution indirectly by checking side-effects (cart count, prefilled fields, search value). Test medicine TEST_HID_001 (id starts with c1480edf) is persistent — reuse it. The camera-scanner modal is opened via testID `btn-open-scanner` on /sell; there is no dedicated close-testID but Escape or clicking outside works.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no defects identified. Design note for main agent: the web-build listener attaches to `document` and captures EVERY keydown, then discards non-scanner traffic by the 60ms rule. If a screen ever mounts a TextInput that legitimately handles fast programmatic input (e.g. paste-heavy fields), the scanner may still fire because paste doesn't dispatch keydown per char — so this is safe. However, if the app ever adds a barcode-INPUT field where the user might tap-and-type quickly, consider gating with `document.activeElement.tagName !== 'INPUT'` to prevent false positives. Not blocking for this release.
